frequency: Repeat every 5 minutes if no response
remarks: Most important intervention. Adults 0.5 mg, children 0.01 mg/kg max 0.5 mg. Do NOT delay for IV; IM thigh.
Adult 200 mg IV; paeds 4 mg/kg max 200 mg. Adjunct only — adrenaline is primary.
Symptomatic relief. Not first-line. Adult 10 mg; child 1 mo-1 yr 250 mcg/kg; 1-5 yr 2.5 mg; 6-11 yr 5 mg.
Refractory shock after IM adrenaline + fluid. Cardiac monitor + ICU. 0.1–1 mcg/kg/min titrated.
Adult 5 mg/neb; child < 5 yr 2.5 mg, ≥ 5 yr 5 mg. Repeat as needed.
4–10 puffs via spacer (more accessible than nebuliser; equally effective). Repeat q20 min × 1h.
Add to salbutamol for severe attacks. Child 250 mcg, adult 500 mcg.

preparation: 5 mg tablet or 15 mg/5 mL syrup
remarks: Adult 40-50 mg/d × 5 days. Child 1-2 mg/kg/d max 40 mg × 3-5 days. No taper for short course.

preparation: 4 mg tablet or 2 mg/5 mL syrup
remarks: Alternative to prednisolone — better tolerance, single dose, equivalent efficacy in paeds. 0.3-0.6 mg/kg × 1-2 doses.
For severe attack not responding. Adult 2 g IV over 20 min; child 40-50 mg/kg max 2 g.
If unable to take oral. Adult 100-200 mg IV q6h; child 4 mg/kg max 100-200 mg q6h.
WHO 2014 — 3 days for non-severe; 5 days if severe. 40-50 mg/kg/dose BD.
Severe pneumonia (chest indrawing or danger signs). 50 mg/kg IV q6h + gentamicin.
With ampicillin for severe paediatric pneumonia. 7.5 mg/kg/day OD. Monitor for ototoxicity if > 5 days.
Treatment failure or very severe. 50-80 mg/kg/day OD. Add cloxacillin/vancomycin if Staph suspected.
Children < 20 kg: 3 mg/kg/dose (higher per kg PK). Minimum 3 IV doses; complete with oral ACT × 3 days when tolerating PO. Watch delayed haemolysis 7-21 days.
If artesunate unavailable. Loading 20 mg/kg over 4h then 10 mg/kg q8h. Cardiac monitor — hypoglycaemia + arrhythmia. Switch to oral when able.
Children: 5 mL/kg of 10% dextrose for BG < 2.2 mmol/L. Frequent monitoring.
Weight-banded: 5-14 kg 1 tab; 15-24 kg 2; 25-34 kg 3; ≥ 35 kg 4 tabs per dose. Take with fat. NOT first trimester pregnancy.
First trimester pregnancy. Quinine 10 mg/kg q8h × 7 days + clindamycin 10 mg/kg q12h × 7 days.
0.05-0.1 U/kg/h. Start AFTER initial 1h fluid. Continue basal long-acting insulin if previously on. Switch SC when ketones < 0.5 + pH > 7.3.
SHOCK only — 10-20 mL/kg over 30-60 min. Then maintenance + replace deficit (max 5-10%) over 48h SLOWLY (cerebral oedema risk).
Cerebral oedema (any decline in mental status / pattern of breathing / focal signs). 3% NaCl 5 mL/kg over 10-15 min. Preferred over mannitol in paeds. URGENT CT after stabilising.
Alternative to hypertonic saline. 0.5-1 g/kg IV over 10-15 min for cerebral oedema.
Adult: 4 mg IV (0.1 mg/kg) repeat ×1 if still seizing 5 min after first dose.
No IV access. RAMPART trial — IM midazolam non-inferior to IV lorazepam. Adult 10 mg IM.
60 mg/kg IV over 5 min (max 4500 mg). ESETT NEJM 2019 — equally effective as phenytoin / valproate. Fewer interactions + safer cardiac.
Phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV at MAX 50 mg/min (cardiac toxicity); fosphenytoin safer at 150 mg PE/min. Cardiac monitor.
40 mg/kg IV over 10 min (max 3 g). AVOID pregnancy / WCBP / mitochondrial / liver disease.
0.1 mg/kg IV max 4 mg. Repeat once if seizing 5 min later.
0.3-0.5 mg/kg (max 10 mg). Buccolam is age-banded. Useful in community + pre-hospital.
Older preparation, useful in community.
Especially neonates. 20 mg/kg IV over 20 min. Cardiac + respiratory monitoring (sedation/apnoea).

Adult 2 g q12h IV. With dexamethasone IV 10 mg q6h × 4 days BEFORE/WITH first antibiotic dose (reduces hearing loss + mortality in pneumococcal). Add amoxicillin if Listeria risk (> 50 / immunocompromised / pregnancy).
Add for age > 50, immunocompromised, pregnancy, neonate. 2 g IV q4h × 21 days.
10 mg IV q6h × 4 days. Give BEFORE or WITH first antibiotic dose. Improves outcomes in pneumococcal meningitis.
4.5 g IV q8h (q6h for severe). Within 1 hour. De-escalate per culture. Add vancomycin if MRSA risk.
Loading 25-30 mg/kg IV (max 2 g) then 15-20 mg/kg q12h. Trough monitoring (target 15-20 for severe).
1 g IV q8h. ESBL coverage or pen-allergy. Severe + hospital-acquired.
30 mL/kg over 3 hours if hypotension or lactate > 4. Reassess (passive leg raise) — avoid over-resuscitation.
First-line for septic shock. Start 0.05-0.1 mcg/kg/min, titrate to MAP ≥ 65 mmHg.
300 mg chewed at first medical contact, then 75 mg/d lifelong.
180 mg loading then 90 mg BD × 12 months. Preferred over clopidogrel in most ACS.
During PCI. 70-100 U/kg IV bolus, target ACT 250-300. Or LMWH (enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BD).
Caution if SBP < 90, RV infarct, recent PDE5i.
2-5 mg IV slow boluses (0.1 mg/kg) titrated for ongoing chest pain. Antiemetic adjunct.
Adult 20 mg IV over 2 min, double q10 min up to 80 mg per dose, max 220 mg cumulative; or infusion 0.5-2 mg/min.
5-10 mg IV q15-20 min (pregnancy). Avoid in severe CVD (reflex tachy).
0.25-10 mcg/kg/min. Cyanide toxicity > 24h; arterial line monitoring.
Loading 4 g IV over 5-10 min + maintenance 1 g/h IV × 24h post-delivery / last seizure. Watch toxicity (reflexes, RR, UO). Calcium gluconate 1 g antidote bedside.
20 mg IV, double q10 min, max 220 mg. Target SBP 140-155, DBP 90-105.
10 mg PO (NOT sublingual — uncontrolled drop). Alternative when IV not available.

0.4 mg IV repeat q2-3 min titrated to RR > 12 (not consciousness). Up to 2-10 mg for fentanyl-adulterated. IN 4 mg lay rescuer (Narcan). Watch resedation (especially methadone/SR opioids — observe 24+ h).

preparation: Dilute 2 mg in 500 mL D5W = 4 mcg/mL
remarks: Long-acting opioids (methadone, SR oxycodone, fentanyl patch) — infusion needed. Titrate to RR.
10 mL of 10% Ca gluconate IV over 2-5 min. ONSET 1-3 min, lasts 30-60 min. Does NOT lower K+ — just buys time. Or Ca chloride 10% 10 mL (3× more Ca, prefer central).
10 U short-acting insulin IV + 25 g glucose (50 mL of 50% OR 250 mL of 10%) over 15-30 min. Monitor glucose hourly × 6h (hypoglycaemia at 1-2h common).
10-20 mg neb. Caution IHD.
10 g TDS × 48h then 5-10 mg/d maintenance. Or patiromer 8.4 g/d. Or loop diuretic (furosemide 40 mg IV) if hypervolaemic + functioning kidney. Dialysis if refractory / AKI.
0.9 mg/kg IV (max 90 mg). 10% as bolus, 90% over 60 min. Within 4.5h of onset. BP < 185/110 before; < 180/105 × 24h after. Check contraindications.
0.25 mg/kg IV single bolus (max 25 mg). EXTEND-IA TNK + AcT — non-inferior to alteplase; simpler single bolus.
Target BP < 185/110 before thrombolysis; < 180/105 × 24h after. Labetalol 10-20 mg IV q10 min.
300 mg PO/PR within 48h of stroke onset (24h after tPA if given). Then 75 mg daily long-term.
50-80 mg/kg/day IV OD. Add vancomycin if MRSA risk; anti-pseudo if neutropenic. Within 1 hour.
10-20 mL/kg bolus IV over 5-10 min for SHOCK. Reassess each bolus. FEAST trial — AVOID bolus in non-shock African children (harmful).
0.05-0.3 mcg/kg/min — first-line vasopressor in paediatric septic shock (vs noradrenaline in adults). Peripheral acceptable initially if no central.
50 mg/m²/dose IV q6h × 4 doses if fluid-refractory shock requiring vasopressor (adrenal insufficiency common in critically ill).
50-100 mg/kg q12h (first week); q8h thereafter. Higher dose if meningitis (200-300 mg/kg/d). Treat for 10-14 days standard; 21 days if meningitis.
Term 4-5 mg/kg/day OD; preterm 3-4 mg/kg q24-36h. Monitor for ototoxicity.
10-15 mg/kg/dose (frequency by age + renal function). MRSA / line-associated.
50 mg/kg q8-12h. NICU acquired. Combine with vancomycin.
20 mg/kg q8h × 14 days (skin-eye-mouth) or 21 days (CNS / disseminated). Empirical if HSV suspected — vesicles, maternal genital herpes.
5 mg/kg/d (range 4-6). Add pyridoxine (B6) 10-25 mg/d to prevent peripheral neuropathy.

remarks: 10 mg/kg/d (range 8-12 adult; 15 mg/kg paeds). Major CYP3A4 inducer — DTG dose 50 mg BD when co-administered.
25 mg/kg/d (range 20-30). Hepatotoxic — monitor LFTs.
15-20 mg/kg/d. Visual acuity + colour vision monthly (optic neuropathy).
Continuation 4 months. FDC by weight band per Kenya TIBU. Total 6 months for drug-sensitive TB.
WITHIN 72 hours of exposure. 28 days. Test HIV at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months. Counsel + STI/Hep B/EC if applicable.
2 mg/kg OD × 6 weeks (low-risk HIV-exposed infant). HIGH-RISK (mother diagnosed late / VL not suppressed): NVP + AZT × 12 weeks.

remarks: Plan B: 75 mL/kg over 4 hours via cup + spoon. Continue breastfeeding. Counsel danger signs.
Adults + > 12 mo: 100 mL/kg over 3h (30 mL/kg in first 30 min, then 70 mL/kg in 2.5h). Infants < 12 mo: 30 mL/kg in 1h then 70 mL/kg in next 5h. Continue ORS as soon as able.

Cholera with severe dehydration: aggressive IV resuscitation. Adults 100 mL/kg in 3h. Match ongoing losses 1:1. Plus doxycycline 300 mg single dose adults (or azithromycin 20 mg/kg children/preg) + zinc 20 mg × 10 days.
Adult 8 mg PO/IV pre-chemo, max 16 mg single dose (QT prolongation). ECG check. Constipation common.
125 mg PO day 1, 80 mg days 2-3. For highly emetogenic regimens.
12 mg pre-chemo (or 20 mg if no NK1), 8 mg daily days 2-4.
5-10 mg daily × 4 days (Navari NEJM 2016 — olanzapine quadruplet superior for HEC).
10 IU IM within 1 min of birth (AMTSL). Treatment: 10 IU IM/IV slow + 20 IU in 1L NaCl at 60 drops/min IV.
1 g IV over 10 min within 3 hours of bleeding onset (WOMAN trial). Repeat once after 30 min if bleeding persists.
800 mcg SL — useful if oxytocin unavailable or refractory. Alternative: ergometrine 0.5 mg IM (avoid in hypertension).
100 mcg single dose. Heat-stable preparation preferred for AMTSL where cold chain unreliable (WHO 2018).

preparation: 120 mg/5 mL syrup or 250/500 mg tablet
remarks: 10-15 mg/kg/dose q4-6h. Max 60 mg/kg/24h or 4 g/d adult. Reduce in liver / low weight.

preparation: 100 mg/5 mL syrup or 200/400 mg tablet
remarks: 5-10 mg/kg/dose q6-8h. AVOID in CKD / GI bleed / asthma history / dehydration / < 3 months.
0.3-0.5 mg/kg (age-banded buccolam). If seizing > 5 min. Treat fever + identify cause.
Treat fever for comfort — does NOT prevent recurrence (parental reassurance).

0.1 mg/kg IV titrated. AVOID IM/SC (unpredictable absorption with shock).
For CO poisoning until carboxyhaemoglobin < 5%. Hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV for cyanide (closed-space fire).
Penicillin 2.4 g IV q4h OR Ceftriaxone 2 g IV BD × 7-10 days. Notify public health + contact PEP.
500 mg PO single dose for close contacts (adult). Within 24 hours. Alternative: rifampicin 600 mg BD × 2 days.
1.25-10 mg/d. Target resting HR < 110 lenient / < 80 strict (per symptoms). AVOID in decompensated HF — optimise first.

frequency: IV bolus then infusion or PO
remarks: PO 60-120 mg q8h titrate. IV 0.25 mg/kg over 2 min, repeat 0.35 mg/kg in 15 min; infusion 5-15 mg/h. AVOID in HFrEF.
300 mg IV over 30 min + 900 mg/24h infusion. Then PO load + maintenance. Pulmonary + hepatic + thyroid + skin AEs long-term.
5 mg BD; reduce to 2.5 mg BD if 2 of 3: age ≥ 80, Cr ≥ 133, wt ≤ 60. Best safety profile in elderly + CKD eGFR ≥ 25.
20 mg OD with food. 15 mg if CrCl 15-49. Avoid CrCl < 15.
10 mg BD × 7 days then 5 mg BD (CARAVAGGIO). Extended phase: 2.5 mg BD (AMPLIFY-EXT).
15 mg BD × 21 days then 20 mg OD (SELECT-D). Take with food.
1 mg/kg SC BD (preferred) or 1.5 mg/kg OD. Cancer-associated thrombosis + pregnancy.
100 mg IV over 2 hours OR 10 mg bolus + 90 mg over 2h. Massive PE with haemodynamic instability. Check contraindications.
Start 24/26 BD (or 49/51 if BP tolerates), titrate to 97/103 BD. 36-hour washout if switching from ACE-i.
Start 1.25 mg OD, titrate slowly q2 wk (1.25 → 2.5 → 3.75 → 5 → 7.5 → 10 mg).
25 mg OD, titrate to 50 mg if K+ tolerates. Monitor K+ + Cr (especially elderly + CKD).
10 mg OD. Regardless of diabetes. Hold for surgery 3 days (euglycaemic DKA). Empagliflozin 10 mg/d alternative.
40 mg IV BD if loop-naive; 1-2.5× home oral dose IV if loop-experienced. Or infusion 5-20 mg/h. UO target.
500 mg OD with food, titrate to 500-1000 mg BD with meals. Max 2 g/d. AVOID eGFR < 30; reduce 30-45. Hold for IV contrast + sepsis.
Start 0.25 mg weekly × 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg, titrate q4 wk to 1-2 mg. Pancreatitis, gallbladder. Contraindication: MEN2/MTC.
10 mg OD, titrate 25 mg. HOLD for surgery 3 days (euglycaemic DKA). UTI/genital mycotic — counsel.
Start 0.1-0.2 U/kg/day. Titrate by 2 U every 3 days based on FBG. Target FBG 5-7 mmol/L.

preparation: Glucose tablets / juice / sugar in water
remarks: 15-20 g fast-acting carb. Recheck in 15 min, repeat if still < 4. Long-acting carb after.
Adult 200 mL 10% glucose IV (= 20 g). Child 2-5 mL/kg of 10%. Recheck in 10 min. Maintenance 10% infusion if recurrence.
Adult 1 mg IM/SC; child 0.5 mg if < 25 kg. Response in 10-15 min. Followed by oral carbohydrate when conscious.
80-90 mg/kg/day in 2 doses (high-dose overcomes pneumococcal resistance). 5 d if > 2 yr; 10 d if < 2 yr / severe.
If recent antibiotic / day-care / severe / β-lactamase suspected. 80-90 mg/kg amox component.
10 mg/kg/day × 5 days (day 1: 10 mg/kg; days 2-5: 5 mg/kg).
300/100 mg BD × 5 days within 5 days of symptom onset. Check drug interactions extensively (CYP3A4 — statins, anticoagulants, immunosuppressants). Renal adjust eGFR 30-60.
6 mg PO/IV daily × 10 days for hospitalised + requiring oxygen (RECOVERY trial). Mortality reduction.
1.5 mg PO single dose within 120h (more effective earlier). Can be given OTC + free in many settings.
Most effective EC (> 99%) up to 120h post-exposure. Also ongoing contraception ~ 5-10 years.
30 mg PO single dose within 120h. More effective than levonorgestrel for delayed presentation 72-120h.
Wash wound thoroughly with soap and running water for 15 minutes. Single most important intervention. Then virucidal (70% alcohol / povidone-iodine). Do NOT suture acutely.
WHO-prequalified cell-culture vaccine. Previously vaccinated: 2 doses days 0+3 only (no RIG).
20 IU/kg total. Infiltrate AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE into wound; any remaining IM distant site. Only day 0. Equine RIG alternative: 40 IU/kg.
0.25 mg SC + hydrocortisone 200 mg IV + chlorphenamine 10 mg IV pre-antivenom to reduce reactions.
10 vials IV over 1 hour for systemic envenomation (neurotoxicity, coagulopathy, severe local). Repeat 6h if 20WBCT still abnormal or neurotoxicity persists. Pre-medicate.
Adult: atropine 0.6 mg IV + neostigmine 1.5-2 mg IV (0.025-0.05 mg/kg). Response confirms cobra envenomation.
300 mg OD lifelong (most patients). High genetic barrier + potent. Monitor renal + bone (TAF safer). HIV co-infection: must include 2 anti-HBV in ART (TDF + 3TC/FTC).
One tablet OD × 12 weeks. Pan-genotypic, no genotype testing needed. Cure ≥ 95%. Add ribavirin if decompensated. Check drug interactions (amiodarone, statins, anticonvulsants, rifampicin).
3 tablets daily with food × 8 weeks (no cirrhosis) or 12 weeks (compensated cirrhosis). Cure ≥ 95%.
Start 5 mg/d, titrate to 10 mg after 4-6 weeks. SE: nausea, diarrhoea, bradycardia (ECG + caution syncope history).
Start 5 mg/d, titrate +5 mg/week to 20 mg/d. Combine with ChEI for moderate-severe AD.
WHO 40 mg/kg single dose; repeat in 4-6 wk if heavy infection or persistent symptoms. Safe in pregnancy + lactation (WHO 2006).
Higher dose (60 mg/kg) for S. japonicum + mekongi divided across same day. With food.

diagnosis: Lymphatic filariasis (IDA MDA where Loa absent)
remarks: WHO 200 μg/kg = 0.2 mg/kg single dose with DEC + albendazole (IDA triple). NOT in Loa-endemic areas (encephalopathy).

diagnosis: Lymphatic filariasis (IDA MDA where Loa absent)
remarks: 6 mg/kg single dose with IVM + ALB. CONTRAINDICATED in Loa loa co-endemic and onchocerciasis.

diagnosis: Lymphatic filariasis (IDA MDA where Loa absent)
remarks: Flat 400 mg single dose (regardless of weight) with IVM + DEC.
CDTI 150 μg/kg = 0.15 mg/kg. In Loa-endemic areas TEST first; > 30,000 mf/mL contraindicated (encephalopathy).
10 mg/kg single dose (WHO 2010 — ≥ 95% cure).
20 mg/kg/day × 17 d with paromomycin (WHO/MSF combination). ECG + LFT + amylase monitor.
15 mg/kg/day IM × 17 d with SSG. Audiometry baseline if available.
30 mg/kg total (5 mg/kg × 6 doses over 10 d). Preferred HIV + pregnancy + East Africa where available.
20 mg/kg/day × 20 d Old World / × 28 d New World. ECG + LFT + amylase + FBC monitor for cardiotoxicity.
600 mg adult (450 mg if < 35 kg) monthly supervised × 6 mo. Free WHO MDT blister pack.
100 mg/d adult (50 mg if < 35 kg). G6PD test before — haemolysis risk.
RIF 600 mg + clofazimine 300 mg monthly supervised + DAP 100 mg + clofazimine 50 mg daily × 12 mo. Counsel skin pigmentation transient.
Single dose: 600 mg ≥ 35 kg, 450 mg 25-34 kg, 300 mg 15-24 kg, 150 mg < 15 kg. Reduces leprosy in contacts 57% (LPEP/COLEP).

preparation: Suspension 200 mg/5 mL or tablet 250 mg
remarks: 20 mg/kg single dose max 1 g annually × 3-5 yr MDA at district TF ≥ 5%. Tetracycline 1% eye ointment BD × 6 wk alternative.
Start 20 mg/kg titrate to MTD 35 mg/kg (max ~2 g). FBC q4 wk titration then q3 mo. From age 9 mo per BABY-HUG + REACH SSA. Reduces VOC + ACS + transfusion + mortality + malaria.
125 mg BD < 3 yr, 250 mg BD 3-5 yr. Reduces pneumococcal sepsis 84% (PROPS). Continue longer if splenectomised.
Ceftriaxone 50-80 mg/kg/day + azithromycin 10 mg/kg/d (max 500 mg). Simple transfusion early; exchange if severe. O2 + incentive spirometer + bronchodilator + pain control.
40 mg/d × 4 d (ASH 2019 preferred). Faster + equivalent + less prolonged steroid than pred 1 mg/kg taper.
1 g/kg (×1-2 doses) when rapid response needed (bleeding, pregnancy, pre-op). Watch for AKI + thrombosis + aseptic meningitis.

frequency: 1 mg stat → 0.5 mg at 1 h → 0.5 mg BD-TDS
remarks: 1 mg stat then 0.5 mg at 1 h then 0.5 mg BD-TDS × 3-5 d. Renal-adjust + statin/macrolide/grapefruit interaction. Continue any existing ULT.
30-40 mg/d × 5 d. Use when NSAID + colchicine contraindicated. HF caution.
Start 100 mg (50 mg if CKD) titrate q2-4 wk to TARGET urate < 360 μmol/L (< 300 if tophi). HLA-B*58:01 test before in Han Chinese/Korean/Thai (DRESS).
500-1000 mg IV OD × 3 d then oral pred 60 mg/d. START IMMEDIATELY on clinical suspicion — do not wait for biopsy. Add ASA 75 + PPI + bone protection.
12.5-25 mg/d × 2-4 wk → reduce 2.5 mg q2-4 wk to 10 mg × 4-6 wk → 1 mg q4-8 wk. Total 1-2 yr. Bisphosphonate + Ca + D + PPI cover.
Standard 10 mg OD → up-dose to 4× (40 mg/d) before adding omalizumab. Loratadine 10 / fexofenadine 180 / bilastine 20 / levocetirizine 5 alternatives. Avoid sedating 1st-gen.
Bevacizumab 1.25 mg / ranibizumab 0.5 mg / aflibercept 2 mg per injection (specialist only). CATT/IVAN — bevacizumab equivalent + cheaper SSA. Protocol S/T for DR/DMO. STERILE technique.
1 mg/kg/d (max 60 mg) × 7-14 d then taper. Start within 14 d of symptom onset (window). Intratympanic dexamethasone alternative/salvage. MRI IAM to exclude retrocochlear.
